Explicitly classify the missing active control-plane families, including TASK-081 Admission Failure v2 and TASK-085 Correction Preflight, as consumed through the exact pinned kernel when applicable; explicitly classify TASK-084/A6 under the optional/not-applicable outer-automation boundary unless Python Agent deliberately adopts that surface. finding.issue: The adoption registry claims an upstream audit through authored TASK-103 and TASK-192 requires every currently relevant AIOS architecture/correction family at that checkpoint to receive an explicit adoption classification so future Brain Sync cannot silently forget it. The registry does not satisfy that completeness claim. At the exact upstream audit checkpoint 7d0bbcbce4b1bfeaa47634f9069a8ae9ac44930c, canonical AIOS roadmap state records Admission Failure v2/TASK-081 and Correction Preflight/TASK-085 as completed items in the active control-plane closure sequence, and A6 automated REVIEW-to-REMEDIATION wakeup/TASK-084 as completed parallel outer automation. None of TASK-081, TASK-085, or TASK-084 appears in any capability_families entry. The focused governance regression likewise asserts a selected subset of tasks and therefore passes while those canonical capability families are absent. This recreates the class of omission TASK-192 is specifically intended to prevent: a future Brain can read a registry marked through TASK-103 and still miss architecture that the exact upstream roadmap says exists.
